practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes the ACGME Transitional Year educational programme?

options.text: A one-year independent ABMS board-certification programme.
A 12-month broad-based programme in multiple clinical disciplines that can prepare for a specific future specialty or fundamental clinical education.
A nonclinical research fellowship with no patient-care requirements.
A generic name for any preliminary year without specialty requirements.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACGME Transitional Year requirements define a broad-based programme in multiple clinical disciplines and require a 12-month programme. The description does not create an independent ABMS certification pathway.

practiceQuestions.stem: Under the current Transitional Year requirements, what is the minimum duration of fundamental clinical-skills rotations?

options.text: 12 weeks
16 weeks
24 weeks
36 weeks

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME requirement 4.11.a requires at least 24 weeks of FCS rotations in the listed primary specialties or primary critical-care experiences.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which CHA Transitional Year public-curriculum statement is accurately characterized?

options.text: Every resident is guaranteed exactly 12 weeks of inpatient medicine.
The published sample schedule lists 10–12 weeks of inpatient medicine and 8 weeks of elective time.
The programme has no emergency medicine rotation.
The schedule is a board-certification blueprint.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CHA labels the schedule a sample and lists ranges, including 10–12 inpatient-medicine weeks and 8 elective weeks. It is neither an individual guarantee nor a board blueprint.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional first-year learner is handing off a patient whose status may be worsening. Which I-PASS element specifically asks the receiving clinician to summarize what was heard and ask questions?

options.text: Illness severity
Action list
Situation awareness and contingency planning
Synthesis by receiver

practiceQuestions.rationale: AHRQ defines the final S as synthesis by receiver: the receiver summarizes, asks questions, and restates key actions.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which practice is consistent with CDC core infection-prevention guidance for injection and medication safety?

options.text: Reuse a syringe for the same patient if a new needle is attached.
Use needles and syringes for one patient only, including prefilled syringes and insulin pens.
Bring a multidose vial into every patient room for convenience.
Wash gloves and reuse them if not visibly soiled.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC core practices state that needles and syringes are for one patient only and also set limits for multidose-vial use and glove reuse.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult is being evaluated for possible sepsis without shock. Which statement matches the cited Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidance?

options.text: Use qSOFA alone as the single screening tool.
Do not consider noninfectious causes until cultures return.
Rapidly assess infectious and noninfectious causes and continuously re-evaluate; qSOFA alone is not recommended as the single screening tool.
An archived lecture replaces local sepsis policy and supervising-team input.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2021 guideline recommends against qSOFA as a single screening tool and emphasizes rapid assessment, reassessment, and alternative diagnoses. This question does not provide a treatment order.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which sequence best reflects how the CDC adult immunization schedule instructs clinicians to use the schedule?

options.text: Pick a vaccine from an archived lecture, then ignore conditions and precautions.
Determine age-based recommendations, assess medical-condition indications, then review notes and contraindications/precautions.
Use only the consumer easy-read page.
Treat a missing record as proof that every vaccine is contraindicated.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The current CDC page directs clinicians to determine age recommendations, assess medical conditions, and review notes and contraindications/precautions. Actual recommendations require the current schedule and local clinical context.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner plans a diagnostic-radiology advanced residency after a Transitional Year. Which boundary is correctly stated in ACGME prerequisite guidance?

options.text: Any online course can replace the prerequisite clinical year.
The prerequisite year must include at least 36 weeks of direct patient care, and radiology-related electives have specific limits and supervision conditions.
No direct patient care is required.
A Transitional Year itself certifies diagnostic radiology practice.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACGME prerequisite document specifies 36 weeks of direct patient care and conditions/limits on radiology-related electives for diagnostic radiology. The intended advanced programme and its board retain the eligibility decision.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the most appropriate independent-study QI project input?

options.text: Export a real patient list to a personal spreadsheet.
Use a synthetic/de-identified process map, name a process and balancing measure, and obtain institutional supervision before any live project.
Change an EHR order set without local authorization.
Claim the project meets ACGME scholarly requirements automatically.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Independent work must protect privacy and cannot substitute for local governance. ACGME requirements address quality/safety competencies and CHA publicly lists scholarly work, but neither grants approval to conduct a project.

practiceQuestions.stem: Why are the UCSF Grand Rounds recordings counted as foundation time rather than Transitional-Year specialty time in this course ledger?

options.text: They are unusable because all video lectures are prohibited.
They are general medicine recordings relevant to broad PGY-1 foundations, but they are not identified as CHA Transitional Year lectures or a separate Transitional-Year board curriculum.
Their durations are estimates rather than observed metadata.
They confer ACGME rotation credit.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The UCSF series is an internal-medicine Grand Rounds archive. The ledger uses observed public playlist durations and labels all 41 recordings as foundation, not institutional TY curriculum or rotation credit.

title: Abdominal Imaging Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (Emory offering explicitly non-accredited; independent self-study supplemental course)-aligned independent study

prerequisites.intendedLearner: Radiology physicians, residents and fellows with prior medical-school and diagnostic imaging foundations; Emory describes a physician fellowship but its public page does not publish applicant eligibility details.
assumedKnowledge: medical terminology, clinical history and differential diagnosis
prerequisites.level: Advanced postgraduate self-study; not entry-level medical education.
prerequisites.notEligibility: These learning prerequisites are not Emory admission requirements, ACGME requirements, ABR requirements or proof of competence.

objectives: Choose/justify abdominal imaging modalities and protocols from a clinical question, patient factors, technical adequacy and current guidance.
Interpret abdominal CT, MRI, ultrasound, radiography and fluoroscopy with a systematic search pattern and a prioritized differential.
Apply pattern-based reasoning to hepatobiliary, pancreatic, bowel/peritoneal, GU, pelvic, transplant, trauma and postoperative findings.
Use standardized reporting systems only in the population/organ for which they apply; distinguish LI-RADS, PI-RADS and Bosniak.
Recognize radiation, contrast, MR and procedural safety issues and escalate through local policy rather than infer unsupervised authorization.
Communicate critical findings, uncertainty and evidence-grounded next steps; appraise clinical guidelines and reflect on learning gaps.

units.title: Abdominal imaging workflow, anatomy, and protocol selection
objectives: Translate the clinical question, prior imaging, and patient factors into a defensible modality/protocol choice using current appropriateness guidance.
Use a repeatable search pattern across peritoneal spaces, solid organs, bowel, vessels, bones, and devices; identify incidental/critical findings and communicate urgency.

Explain key CT phases, MRI sequence families, ultrasound Doppler principles, fluoroscopic study purposes, artifacts, and limitations without presenting a self-study protocol as clinical authorization.
topics: CT attenuation, phase timing and multiplanar reconstruction
MRI T1/T2, diffusion, in/opposed phase, dynamic enhancement, MRCP
protocoling, prior comparison, structured report and critical results
units.casePractice: On linked educational cases, write a clinical question, modality selection, protocol rationale, three-step search, one prioritized finding and a communication escalation statement. Use no patient records.
units.assessment: 15-item anatomy/modality quiz plus two annotated, citation-backed structured-report exercises; rubric: modality rationale 30%, search completeness 25%, finding/differential 25%, safety/communication 20%.

units.title: CT, MRI, ultrasound physics, contrast and safety
objectives: Identify acquisition/reconstruction factors that affect image quality and abdominal artifacts.
Apply safety screening concepts for iodinated/gadolinium contrast, MR environments, ultrasound and radiation optimization; defer clinical decisions to current local policies and qualified teams.
Distinguish interpretive educational review from authority to protocol or administer contrast.
topics: iodinated/gadolinium contrast reactions and renal considerations using current manual
Doppler, elastography/CEUS overview; CT colonography preparation and limits
units.casePractice: Use a fictional checklist scenario to find missing MR/contrast safety information; list when to stop and escalate to institutional safety/contrast policy.
units.assessment: Safety station scored pass/fail on identifying screening gaps and escalation; short answer on CT/MR artifact recognition, rubric: accuracy 60%, limits/escalation 40%.

units.title: Liver: diffuse disease, focal lesions, HCC and LI-RADS
objectives: Differentiate common benign, malignant, vascular, inflammatory and diffuse liver imaging patterns across modalities.
Choose characterization imaging for an incidental lesion in context of prior test, background liver and known extrahepatic cancer.
Apply LI-RADS only to its validated at-risk populations, describe category uncertainty and avoid treating a category as pathology.
topics: CT/MR/CEUS dynamic enhancement and ancillary features
LI-RADS scope and reporting; transplant-related findings
units.casePractice: Compare 3 linked liver cases with case-specific context; identify if LI-RADS applies, provide prioritized differential and next imaging question. Do not copy images.
units.assessment: Three vignette interpretations; rubric: context/scope of LI-RADS 35%, enhancement reasoning 35%, differential and recommendation 20%, uncertainty 10%.

units.title: Biliary tree and gallbladder
objectives: Recognize acute/chronic gallbladder inflammation, stones, obstruction, ductal variants, PSC patterns and postoperative changes.
Describe modality strengths/limits and when targeted ultrasound, CT, MRI/MRCP or fluoroscopy may answer a distinct question.
Communicate urgent obstructive/infectious findings without overcalling from isolated imaging signs.
topics: gallbladder neoplasm and postoperative biliary anatomy
units.casePractice: Use a linked gallbladder/intestinal ultrasound teaching case: list observed signs, differential and one needed clinical/lab correlation.
units.assessment: Case-based report and modality-choice MCQ; rubric: signs 40%, differential 25%, modality limits 20%, communication 15%.

units.title: Pancreas: inflammation, neoplasia, cysts and transplant
objectives: Recognize acute/chronic pancreatitis and common complications while distinguishing diagnostic imaging from severity/timing decisions.
Compare pancreas-protocol CT and MRI/MRCP for solid and cystic lesions, ductal anatomy and staging questions.
Describe cyst morphology and risk features with guideline qualification; recommend multidisciplinary correlation rather than unsourced treatment.
topics: PDAC and neuroendocrine tumor staging/resectability descriptors
units.casePractice: On fictional cyst vignettes, map morphology and duct findings to ACR imaging-choice table and state what cannot be decided from size alone.
units.assessment: Structured pancreas report and 10-item quiz; rubric: anatomy 20%, lesion features 35%, staging/complication 25%, qualified recommendation 20%.

units.title: Bowel, mesentery, peritoneum and acute abdomen
objectives: Recognize common obstruction, inflammatory/infectious, neoplastic, ischemic, perforation and postoperative patterns.
Use patient context and ACR guidance to select/qualify cross-sectional versus US/fluoroscopic evaluation.
Search mesentery, peritoneum, hernia sites, bowel enhancement and free air/fluid systematically.
topics: small/large bowel obstruction and transition point
peritoneal disease, collections, hernias and surgery
units.casePractice: Review public case links for obstruction or RLQ pain; draw an anonymized diagram from memory, report transition point/complications and request appropriate clinical escalation.
units.assessment: Timed search-pattern worksheet + paired case discussion; rubric: completeness 30%, differential 25%, complications 25%, communication 20%.

units.title: GU, adrenal, kidneys, urinary tract and prostate interface
objectives: Describe renal mass/cystic lesion characterization, stone/obstruction, adrenal incidentaloma and urothelial imaging patterns at radiologist learning level.
Select CT/MR/US/urographic technique based on clinical question and risk, using current appropriateness guidance.
Correctly distinguish PI-RADS (prostate) from LI-RADS (liver) and Bosniak renal cystic mass classification.
topics: adrenal lesion basics and pheochromocytoma caution
units.casePractice: Annotate a linked renal/prostate case with system applicability, acquisition limits and a concise differential; do not claim histology from score alone.
units.assessment: Cross-system mapping quiz plus structured renal/prostate report; rubric: correct classification 40%, morphology 30%, modality choice 20%, caveats 10%.

units.title: Pelvic, gynecologic, obstetric and pelvic floor imaging
objectives: Recognize common pelvic US/MRI anatomy and findings relevant to adnexal mass, endometriosis, uterine pathology and pelvic floor questions.
Use pregnancy status and acuity to frame modality selection and safety discussion.
Describe hysterosalpingography, defecography and MR defecography as examinations requiring credentialed clinical practice.
units.casePractice: Build a modality-choice matrix for fictional pelvic pain presentations at different pregnancy/acuity states; cite the applicable ACR topic.
units.assessment: Written case set: modality choice 30%, key differential 30%, safety/pregnancy caveats 25%, report clarity 15%.

units.title: Transplant, oncology, trauma and postoperative abdomen
objectives: Identify expected versus concerning imaging findings after abdominal surgery and transplantation.
Organize trauma interpretation around injury, vascular involvement, active bleeding, free air/fluid and limitations.
Present imaging findings in multidisciplinary context without asserting management beyond evidence and team review.
topics: tumor board communication and response comparison
units.casePractice: Compare linked educational transplant/trauma cases; prepare a critical-result verbal handoff using fictional data only.
units.assessment: Image interpretation and handoff station; rubric: anatomy/complication 40%, prioritized differential 25%, urgency 20%, clear limitation 15%.

units.title: Fluoroscopy, CT colonography and specialized abdominal techniques
objectives: Explain indications and limitations of routine fluoroscopic GI/GU examinations, CT colonography and advanced post-processing.
Recognize normal postoperative anatomy and common complications on luminal studies.
Separate didactic exposure from supervised image acquisition, patient consent and procedure competency.
units.casePractice: Create a test selection flowchart and identify three scenarios where a different modality or escalation is warranted.
units.assessment: Diagram plus short oral defense; rubric: purpose 30%, limitations 30%, safety 20%, communication 20%.

units.title: Quality, communication, evidence use and professional practice
objectives: Produce concise findings/impression with pertinent positives, meaningful negatives, differential, uncertainty and actionable next steps.
Use evidence and local policy to communicate critical results and prevent error; understand that ACGME milestones are a competency framework, not an independent credential.
Recognize scope limits, conflicts, bias and patient privacy obligations.
topics: ethics, privacy, informed consent, equity and professionalism
units.casePractice: Audit three fictional reports for ambiguity and create revised impressions with one-line evidence justification and recipient/escalation path.
units.assessment: Report-revision assignment; rubric: clarity 30%, prioritization 25%, evidence 20%, communication 15%, privacy/scope 10%.

units.title: Integrated case conference and board-domain synthesis
objectives: Synthesize abdominal GI, GU, ultrasound, physics and noninterpretive content into an oral case-based approach.
Prioritize time-sensitive findings, offer a focused differential, select a next study when justified, and state uncertainty.
Use ABR published domain maps as exam-scope reference while recognizing current exam format changes and no separate abdominal-imaging exam.
topics: reflective gap analysis and study plan
units.casePractice: Complete a linked public image case as a written and oral report; cite one current guideline and self-identify unresolved areas.
units.assessment: Capstone: two integrated cases and reflective gap log. Rubric: search/diagnosis 35%, differential 20%, next-step reasoning 15%, communication 15%, safety/evidence 15%.

assignment.title: Abdominal imaging portfolio (fictional educational exercises only)
deliverables: Two structured fictional case reports (one liver, one pancreas/bowel or GU) citing a current authoritative imaging recommendation.
One modality/protocol decision matrix with contextual variables and limitations.
One safety checklist exercise (MR/contrast/radiation) and a fictional critical-result handoff.
Capstone reflection that distinguishes confident observation, inference, uncertainty and supervised competency still needed.

rubric.passingCriterion: Suggested learning threshold 80% with mandatory correction of any critical safety/scope error; not a validated board predictor.

assignment.caseAndImageRule: Use only linked public educational cases under their own terms. Do not download, copy, embed or redistribute images or real records. Constructed vignette facts are labelled fictional; no invented patient images or purported case volumes.

assessment.format: Formative quizzes, linked-case worksheets, reporting assignments, oral handoff simulation and integrated capstone.
assessment.practiceQuestionNotice: Original educational questions only; not ABR items, official exam content, validated assessment or predictor of passing.
assessment.weighting: Unit quizzes/case exercises 40%; written portfolio 30%; capstone case conference 20%; reflection 10%.
assessment.clinicalReview: Human clinical review has not been performed; learners should verify current guidance and seek qualified supervision.

studyHours.plan: Planning estimate: 36 hours of unique recorded lecture at target, plus approximately 45–65 hours for readings, case review, assignments and review; about 81–101 total self-study hours. These are study-planning estimates, not claimed clinical training or measured videos. Current ready recordings provide only 6.246944 hours; planned clips do not count.
studyHours.recommendedSequence: Complete prerequisites and unit 1–2 first; units 3–10 in sequence; units 11–12 and capstone last; re-check sources before clinical use.

mapping.name: Abdominal Imaging Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Emory’s official programme page says “one-year non-accredited fellowship position” and describes supervised clinical training across CT/CTA, abdominal and pelvic MRI, PET/MRI collaboration, ultrasound, radiography, fluoroscopy; six weeks elective; dedicated didactics, interesting case conference and tumor boards; research encouraged. Page also names transplant/cancer/ED/trauma clinical context. It does not publish a week-by-week didactic syllabus, exact case volumes, board eligibility requirements, or individual training outcomes. Emory directory is a broad fellowship directory and says its offerings include accredited and non-accredited advanced fellowships; the fellowship page supplies the exact status. ACGME’s Abdominal Radiology requirements/milestones exist as general accreditation standards but do not make this specific Emory position accredited.

topicGaps: The target is 36 verified free recorded hours; the current unique observed-duration ledger is 7.5894444444 hours, leaving 28.4105555556 hours. No target minutes or scripts count as ready video.

Verified recordings remain limited in renal cyst/Bosniak, prostate MRI, gynecologic and obstetric pelvis, transplant, trauma, postoperative complications, fluoroscopy, CT colonography, advanced Doppler, structured reporting and quality improvement.
The added CT and inflammatory recordings expand units 1 and 6, but do not supply complete unit instruction; the brief MRI anatomy video is only a short foundation item.

Five complete source-backed teaching episodes add material in CT search, pancreatic cyst reasoning, adrenal variant selection, acute pelvic-pain modality logic, and MR/contrast safety escalation. They are scripts, not rendered media.

The public Emory description does not give a complete didactic syllabus or clinical case volumes. Public source coverage is insufficient to claim that the 28.4105555556-hour verified-media residual is fulfilled; gaps remain explicit.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

officialProgrammes.name: Abdominal Imaging Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Emory’s official programme page says “one-year non-accredited fellowship position” and describes supervised clinical training across CT/CTA, abdominal and pelvic MRI, PET/MRI collaboration, ultrasound, radiography, fluoroscopy; six weeks elective; dedicated didactics, interesting case conference and tumor boards; research encouraged. practiceQuestions.stem: A 1.6-cm indeterminate lesion was found on ultrasound in a patient with a normal liver and no known extrahepatic malignancy. Which characterization options are rated usually appropriate by ACR in this scenario?

options.text: US with IV contrast, MRI abdomen without and with IV contrast, or multiphase CT abdomen with IV contrast.
Immediate biopsy as the only recommended step.
Noncontrast CT alone.
PSMA PET/CT.

practiceQuestions.rationale: For this exact variant, ACR lists contrast-enhanced US, MRI without/with contrast, and multiphase CT as usually appropriate. Other factors can change the choice; biopsy is not the only route.

practiceQuestions.stem: A lesion is seen on a single-phase CT in a patient with no known malignancy or chronic liver disease. Which next study is usually appropriate in ACR’s defined scenario?

options.text: MRI without and with IV contrast or multiphase CT with IV contrast.
No additional imaging ever.
CT without contrast only.
Routine colonoscopy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACR rates MRI without/with contrast and multiphase CT with IV contrast usually appropriate when the initial study was single-phase CT/noncontrast MRI in the specified normal-liver/no-cancer scenario.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about LI-RADS is most accurate?

options.text: It is a universal malignancy score for every liver lesion in any patient.
It is used in defined at-risk populations and should not be applied outside its scope or to inadequate studies.
It is the standard classification for prostate MRI.
A category substitutes for histology in every setting.

practiceQuestions.rationale: LI-RADS is intended for standardized reporting in defined populations at risk for HCC; population and technical eligibility matter. PI-RADS is prostate, and scores are not histology.

practiceQuestions.stem: An incidental pancreatic cyst <=2.5 cm is identified. Which modality does the ACR criterion rate usually appropriate for initial evaluation?

options.text: MRI abdomen without and with IV contrast with MRCP.
Unenhanced abdominal radiograph.
PET/CT for all cases.
Immediate endoscopic ultrasound in every case.

practiceQuestions.rationale: For its defined initial evaluation variant for cyst <=2.5 cm, ACR rates MRI with/without contrast and MRCP usually appropriate. This does not alone define management or surveillance for every person.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which ACR statement is given for a >2.5-cm pancreatic cyst with high-risk stigmata or worrisome features on initial evaluation?

options.text: MRI with MRCP and endoscopic ultrasound are rated usually appropriate.
Imaging is never appropriate.
Only noncontrast CT is appropriate.
Radiologic size alone establishes benignity.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACR rates MRI/MRCP and endoscopic ultrasound usually appropriate in this defined scenario. Clinical and multidisciplinary assessment remain necessary.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which classification belongs to prostate MRI, not liver or renal cystic mass assessment?

options.text: PI-RADS.
LI-RADS.
Bosniak.
Lung-RADS.

practiceQuestions.rationale: PI-RADS is the prostate imaging reporting system; LI-RADS concerns liver in defined settings, while Bosniak is for cystic renal masses.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the most defensible first step when interpreting a complex abdominal study?

options.text: State a diagnosis before reviewing the clinical question or images.
Confirm clinical context, comparison, coverage and technical adequacy, then use a systematic search.
Ignore prior imaging.
Treat a single incidental finding as pathognomonic.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A structured interpretation begins with question/context and technical adequacy and uses systematic search and comparisons. Avoid diagnostic anchoring and unsupported certainty.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with an unidentified implant is scheduled for abdominal MRI. Which response is safest in an educational scenario?

options.text: Proceed if the requested exam is abdominal.
Follow the institutional MR screening process and obtain device-specific safety review before scanning.
Assume every implant is MR Safe.
Use oral contrast to neutralize magnetic risk.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Implant/foreign body status requires screening and evaluation under current MR safety procedures. This course does not authorize scanning or replace a qualified MR safety team.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes a recorded lecture duration in this curriculum?

options.text: It proves educational quality and persistent access.
It records an observed public-player runtime on the check date; availability may change and viewing does not imply rehosting rights.
It can be estimated from video title.
A playlist total may be multiplied by replaying the same videos.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Ledger durations are observed, unique recording runtimes; they do not establish quality, permanence, accreditation, or redistribution rights.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is true about Emory’s listed Abdominal Imaging Fellowship and ABR certification based on official pages checked 2026-10-07?

options.text: Emory describes a one-year non-accredited fellowship; ABR subspecialty certification categories do not list abdominal imaging as a separate exam.
It is a three-year residency conferring a separate abdominal board.
It is a generic non-physician imaging directory category.
Completion guarantees DR board eligibility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Emory expressly calls it a one-year non-accredited fellowship. ABR’s current listed DR/IR subspecialty certifications include neuroradiology, nuclear radiology, pediatric radiology, pain medicine—not abdominal imaging. This does not determine an individual’s DR eligibility.

title: Breast Imaging Fellowship
prerequisites: For the intended advanced learner: prior diagnostic-radiology residency-level understanding of anatomy, radiation safety, mammographic positioning, US and MRI fundamentals, image interpretation, pathology correlation and patient communication. This is a knowledge prerequisite, not an admission or credential requirement.

Ability to read current primary sources and distinguish screening, diagnostic evaluation, appropriateness guidance, regulatory requirements and institutional policy. Learners must compare older recordings with current FDA, ACR and USPSTF sources.

No learner may independently interpret examinations, administer contrast, perform localizations/biopsies/drainage/cryoablation, access clinical systems, or treat a patient through this curriculum. Such activities require applicable licensure, supervision, facility policy, credentialing and patient-specific judgment.
objectives: Explain the breast-imaging fellowship scope, the ABR DR boundary, and the distinction among a fellowship, certification, accreditation, MQSA qualification and independent study.
Compare screening and diagnostic mammography/DBT, US, MRI and contrast-enhanced mammography using current source-specific indication and evidence limits.
Use a structured, authorized reporting workflow that separates observed finding, technical adequacy, comparison, assessment and communication; do not reproduce proprietary BI-RADS Atlas content.
Reason through age- and scenario-specific diagnostic work-up of a palpable concern using ACR appropriateness criteria rather than a one-size-fits-all modality rule.
Explain breast density communication, MQSA quality/audit concepts, and the legal limits on independent mammography interpretation in the United States.
Describe, at a conceptual level, US, MRI, DBT and contrast-enhanced mammography strengths, artifacts, limitations and appropriate correlation pathways.
Plan radiologic-pathologic correlation and multidisciplinary communication, including escalation of discordance to the credentialed clinical team.
Recognize that image-guided breast procedures and MRI/mammography interpretation require supervised clinical training, credentialing and local policy beyond readings, videos and case review.
Use lawfully accessible, de-identified teaching cases with attribution and no re-identification, rehosting or fabricated diagnostic images.

units.title: Scope, evidence hierarchy and screening frameworks
objectives: Separate an institutional fellowship description from ABR certification, ACGME accreditation, MQSA law and independent study.
Contrast USPSTF population-level recommendations with ACR scenario-based appropriateness without treating either as an individualized order.
topics: USPSTF 2024 screening population and evidence-insufficiency statements
units.casePractice: Create a source comparison grid for average-, intermediate- and high-risk screening scenarios. State the population and source before any modality conclusion; do not issue an order.
units.assessment: 400-word evidence reconciliation: identify one agreement and one scope difference between USPSTF and ACR; cite both sources.

units.title: Mammography and DBT: acquisition, quality and systematic review
objectives: Explain the screening versus diagnostic workflow and the role of prior comparison.
Identify why positioning, exposure, image quality, overlap and DBT slice review affect interpretive reliability.
units.casePractice: Using linked-only CBIS-DDSM cases, record a structured technical/observation note without copying image pixels or exporting patient data.
units.assessment: Ten-item image-quality and workflow checklist with a one-sentence reason for each item; peer compare against the ACR practice parameter.

units.title: Risk, density and supplemental imaging reasoning
objectives: Explain density as both a masking and communication issue without promising that one supplemental test fits every person.
Compare ACR appropriateness categories across density/risk variants and the USPSTF evidence boundary.
topics: DBT, MRI, US and contrast mammography
units.casePractice: For three fictional risk/density vignettes, name the relevant ACR variant and one evidence limitation. Do not assign a patient plan.
units.assessment: Short-answer comparison of ACR and USPSTF statements on supplemental US/MRI after a negative mammogram in dense breasts.

units.title: Mammographic findings, assessment and communication
objectives: Describe masses, asymmetries, architectural distortion and calcification patterns in a systematic observation-first workflow.
Explain how final assessment and timely communication are quality/safety issues without reproducing the proprietary BI-RADS Atlas.
units.casePractice: Work through UW case pages in source view and write an original observation/differential note; retain UW attribution and do not rehost images.
units.assessment: Structured report critique: identify missing technical, comparison, communication or follow-up elements in three fictional reports.

units.title: Breast and axillary ultrasound
objectives: Explain US's diagnostic, correlation and intervention roles and its operator-dependent limitations.
Organize a focal US observation using authorized descriptors and correlate with mammography/clinical context.
units.casePractice: Use UW public teaching-file cases to record correlation questions and uncertainty; no images may be copied into a local test bank.
units.assessment: Age-stratified work-up map for a fictional palpable concern, checked against the ACR Palpable Breast Masses variants.

units.title: Contrast-enhanced breast MRI and contrast-enhanced mammography
objectives: Explain MRI enhancement, morphology, background enhancement and correlation at a conceptual level.
Compare MRI and CEM capabilities/constraints while preserving contrast safety, FDA, facility and credential limits.
units.casePractice: Review de-identified TCIA MRI metadata/annotations only under its license and citation rule. Write a modality-correlation question, not a clinical recommendation.
units.assessment: Two-column limitation matrix: MRI, CEM and US; include one technical, one patient-safety and one evidence/credential limitation each.

units.title: Diagnostic presentations and appropriateness pathways
objectives: Use ACR age-stratified pathways for palpable findings without equating screening and diagnostic examinations.
Recognize the need for correlation and escalation when imaging/clinical findings are discordant.
units.casePractice: Choose two UW cases and one fictional symptomatic presentation. For each, state what additional information the credentialed team would need before action.

mapping.name: Breast Imaging Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Emory states it is a one-year programme with six positions per year, weekly breast-imaging lectures and multidisciplinary conferences. Its public curriculum lists screening/diagnostic mammography including DBT, breast ultrasound, MRI interpretation, image-guided localizations and biopsies, abscess drainage, plus exposure to contrast-enhanced mammography and cryoablation. Publicly named rotation sites include Winship Cancer Institute, Winship at Emory University Hospital Midtown, Emory Saint Joseph's, the DeKalb Operating Unit (Emory Decatur/Hillandale), and Georgia Cancer Center for Excellence at Grady. The page says fellows have junior faculty appointments, call and attending backup; this is not a complete schedule, case log or competency record. Emory requires DR board eligibility following an accredited radiology residency and Georgia medical-license eligibility. The page does not state that the fellowship is ACGME-accredited.

mapping.name: Breast Imaging Fellowship

Its applicant/licensure details differ from Emory's: it seeks completed ACGME DR residency and DR board certification/eligibility at onset, and Maryland licensure eligibility for independent call. Public page estimates service volumes but those figures are not course requirements or learner outcomes. These Hopkins details are preserved as its own exact variant and are not attributed to Emory.

boardNames: American Board of Radiology (ABR) — Diagnostic Radiology (DR) certification; breast imaging is a DR examination content domain, not a distinct breast-imaging certificate.
medical.boardStatus: As checked 2026-10-07: there is no separate ABR Breast Imaging subspecialty certificate or board exam. ABR's DR Qualifying (Core) content includes breast imaging, noninterpretive skills and physics; its currently listed DR/IR-DR subspecialty certificates are neuroradiology, nuclear radiology, pain medicine and pediatric radiology. ABR states that after 2027 the general Diagnostic Radiology Oral Exam has a breast clinical category. That is a category of the DR certification process, not a distinct breast-imaging fellowship board. This self-study is only aligned to the published high-level domains and does not establish board eligibility, preparation sufficiency or likelihood of passing.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Both institutional fellowships are post-diagnostic-radiology clinical training, not residency. Emory says fellows must be board-eligible for a DR certificate after an accredited radiology residency and able to obtain a Georgia medical license; Johns Hopkins says candidates should have completed ACGME DR residency and be DR board-certified or board-eligible at fellowship onset, with Maryland license eligibility for independent call. Applicants must check the individual programme and relevant boards/regulators for current eligibility. This independent course cannot establish eligibility, confer ABR certification, satisfy MQSA or ACR credentials, provide licensure, procedure privileges or supervised experience, or guarantee an examination result.

officialProgrammes.name: Breast Imaging Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Emory states it is a one-year programme with six positions per year, weekly breast-imaging lectures and multidisciplinary conferences. Its public curriculum lists screening/diagnostic mammography including DBT, breast ultrasound, MRI interpretation, image-guided localizations and biopsies, abscess drainage, plus exposure to contrast-enhanced mammography and cryoablation. Publicly named rotation sites include Winship Cancer Institute, Winship at Emory University Hospital Midtown, Emory Saint Joseph's, the DeKalb Operating Unit (Emory Decatur/Hillandale), and Georgia Cancer Center for Excellence at Grady. The page says fellows have junior faculty appointments, call and attending backup; this is not a complete schedule, case log or competency record. Emory requires DR board eligibility following an accredited radiology residency and Georgia medical-license eligibility. The page does not state that the fellowship is ACGME-accredited.

officialProgrammes.name: Breast Imaging Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Hopkins separately describes a 12-month clinical breast-imaging fellowship, following ACR/SBI guidelines, with mammography/DBT, ultrasound and MRI, listed image-guided interventions, weekly multidisciplinary conferences, and fellows rotating at Levi Watkins Jr. Outpatient Center and Johns Hopkins Imaging–Green Spring (with visits to other sites possible). Its applicant/licensure details differ from Emory's: it seeks completed ACGME DR residency and DR board certification/eligibility at onset, and Maryland licensure eligibility for independent call. Public page estimates service volumes but those figures are not course requirements or learner outcomes. These Hopkins details are preserved as its own exact variant and are not attributed to Emory.

officialProgrammes.name: Mass General Brigham Breast Imaging Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official directory-listed institutional variant; a full internal rotation or lecture curriculum was not verified in the directory discovery.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The course represents two verified but institutionally distinct one-year clinical physician fellowship offerings—Emory University School of Medicine and Johns Hopkins Medicine—using only each institution's public overview. Shared learning themes are appropriate for the specialty, but the two programmes' sites, schedules, applicant requirements, case exposure, supervision and procedures are not merged or inferred. Neither public overview provides a complete rotation schedule, case log, trainee-specific volume, complete didactic catalogue or individual competency sign-off. Emory does not publicly state ACGME accreditation for this fellowship; the current ACGME radiology page lists programme categories but does not establish this fellowship's status. Rotations are context only and never count as course video hours.
sourceCaveats: The user-provided nuclear-medicine outline is not imported: this entry is breast imaging only. Its unsupported volume/equipment/board claims do not establish this programme's curriculum.

Public videos are supplemental recordings from mixed providers. A visible duration and public watch page establish only a countable recording, not current accuracy, CME, faculty supervision, institutional endorsement or clinical competency.
Public Emory information does not publish a complete lecture timetable, case minimums, trainee-specific rotations or formal clinical competency assessment. No such details are invented.

ACR BI-RADS is proprietary. This course links the official product page and uses lawful high-level reporting concepts; it does not provide a protected atlas/PDF, copied images or proprietary exam material.
ACR, USPSTF, NCI and FDA sources have distinct scope and may differ. The entry preserves the source/population/variant rather than collapsing them into one universal rule.
TCIA collections are research data, not clinical systems; their licenses, citations, tools and data-use restrictions govern use.

Neither public fellowship overview identifies its programme as ACGME-accredited. The current ACGME Radiology requirements page lists several programme categories, but that page is not a programme-specific accreditation verification. Accreditation status for these breast-imaging fellowships is therefore not claimed or inferred.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes ABR breast-imaging certification status as of 2026?

options.text: Breast Imaging has its own ABR subspecialty certificate and separate exam.
Breast imaging is included in DR examination content, but no separate breast-imaging ABR certificate is listed.
Completion of any breast imaging fellowship automatically confers ABR certification.
ABR does not examine breast imaging.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABR lists breast imaging among DR Qualifying (Core) content and lists separate DR/IR-DR subspecialty certificates as neuroradiology, nuclear radiology, pain medicine and pediatric radiology. The general DR Oral Exam after 2027 includes a breast category, not a separate breast certificate.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner compares population screening recommendations for an average-risk population aged 40–74. What does the current USPSTF recommendation state?

options.text: Annual MRI for all patients.
Biennial screening mammography.
No screening before age 50.
Screening ultrasound without mammography.

practiceQuestions.rationale: USPSTF recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 through 74. This population-level recommendation is not a patient-specific order and does not cover all high-risk conditions.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult female younger than 30 presents with a palpable mass and needs initial imaging. Under the corresponding ACR variant, which modality is rated usually appropriate?

options.text: Screening mammography.
Breast ultrasound.
Breast MRI without contrast.
Dedicated FDG-PET breast imaging.

practiceQuestions.rationale: For ACR's defined initial-imaging variant for adult females younger than 30 with a palpable mass, breast ultrasound is rated usually appropriate; this rating does not replace clinical assessment or authorize independent ordering.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult female aged 40 or older presents with a palpable mass. Which initial imaging statement matches the ACR variant?

options.text: Screening mammography is usually appropriate and diagnostic mammography usually not appropriate.
Diagnostic mammography and diagnostic DBT are usually appropriate; ultrasound may be appropriate.
MRI is always the required first study.
No imaging is appropriate.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACR's 40-or-older variant rates diagnostic mammography and diagnostic DBT as usually appropriate and breast US as may be appropriate. Screening mammography is not the same clinical question.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the USPSTF's evidence statement for supplemental ultrasound or MRI after a negative screening mammogram in women with dense breasts?

options.text: Evidence proves both reduce mortality in all women.
Evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms.
Both are prohibited.
MRI is required by federal law.

practiceQuestions.rationale: USPSTF gives an I statement for supplemental US or MRI after a negative mammogram in women with dense breasts. Other bodies may issue scenario-specific appropriateness guidance; preserve the differing source and scope.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which change does FDA identify among amended MQSA requirements enforced beginning September 10, 2024?

options.text: Density is excluded from every mammography report.
Mammography reports include an overall breast-density assessment and patients receive density-specific lay-summary language.
Only research centres are regulated.
All breast imaging requires a new ABR certificate.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA's final-rule information describes overall density assessment in the report and density-specific notification language. This describes facility obligations, not an individual learner's qualification.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the correct interpretation of Emory's published list of breast procedures for a self-study learner?

options.text: The list grants a learner privileges after watching videos.
It describes supervised exposure in an institutional clinical fellowship and does not establish independent procedural competence.
It proves every fellow performs every procedure at a fixed volume.
It is an ABR certification list.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Emory describes procedures in its one-year fellowship curriculum, but does not publish a learner's case log or competency record. Self-study cannot confer supervised experience or privileges.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description correctly distinguishes the two institutional variants in this course?

options.text: Emory and Johns Hopkins share an identical rotation schedule and credential requirements.
They are separately described one-year clinical fellowships; programme-specific sites and eligibility details must remain distinct.
One is a residency and one is a research-only supplement.
Hopkins information can be used as evidence for Emory procedures.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Emory's and Hopkins' official pages independently describe clinical one-year/12-month fellowships while listing institution-specific sites, clinical experience and application/licensure conditions. One programme's public claims cannot be assigned to the other.

practiceQuestions.stem: What does a TCIA collection's public accessibility imply about reuse?

options.text: Images may be republished freely without checking collection terms.
The collection's stated license, citation and data-use rules still govern; free viewing alone is not blanket redistribution permission.
De-identification makes re-identification permissible.
Research labels are equivalent to current clinical diagnoses.

practiceQuestions.rationale: TCIA policies and each collection's license/citation requirements remain applicable. No dataset permits re-identification or patient contact through this course; research cohorts and labels are not current clinical records.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which conclusion follows from public ACGME and institutional programme pages?

options.text: Because no separate Breast Imaging category appears on the ACGME Radiology requirements index, the Emory fellowship is definitively unaccredited.
The ACGME index lists programme requirement categories, but neither its category list nor the Emory overview alone proves the accreditation status of this fellowship.
Every fellowship at Emory is ACGME-accredited.
A public curriculum overview proves every trainee completed identical clinical volume.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACGME page lists named program-requirement categories but is not a programme-specific accreditation determination. The Emory fellowship page does not state ACGME accreditation; status remains unverified from these pages and is not inferred from silence.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional trial baseline CT has multiple solid-tumour lesions. Which statement best reflects RECIST 1.1 target-lesion selection?

options.text: Measure every visible lesion because more measurements always improve reproducibility.
Select up to five total target lesions, with no more than two per organ, representing involved organs; separately document non-target disease.
Select only PET-avid lesions and use SUV as the sole size metric.
Use ultrasound for all measurable lesions because it avoids radiation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: RECIST 1.1 limits target lesions to five total and two per organ, with representative selection; anatomical measurements and separate non-target documentation remain important. PET uptake alone does not replace the framework.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a trial using iRECIST, a scan first meets progression criteria during immunotherapy, while the participant is clinically stable. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.text: iRECIST automatically requires continuing treatment in all patients.

Record immune unconfirmed progressive disease (iUPD); confirmatory assessment and clinical stability are part of the trial framework, while treatment decisions remain with the clinical team and protocol.
Ignore all new lesions until the next annual scan.
Re-label the scan as complete response if there is no symptom change.

practiceQuestions.rationale: iRECIST is a clinical-trial data framework, not a treatment directive. It differentiates iUPD and iCPD and notes clinical stability in decisions about continued therapy under protocol and healthcare-team direction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with FDG-avid lymphoma has serial PET/CT. Which response framework is most appropriate to consider, subject to protocol and disease context?

options.text: PI-RADS.
Lugano classification with FDG-PET/CT and Deauville scoring where applicable.
LI-RADS.
Bosniak cystic renal mass classification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Lugano uses PET/CT in FDG-avid lymphoma response evaluation; other listed systems address prostate, liver, and renal cystic lesions, respectively.

practiceQuestions.stem: A PET/CT shows focal FDG uptake at a site of recent surgery with surrounding inflammatory change. What is the most defensible first interpretive move?

options.text: Call metastatic disease because any focal FDG uptake is malignant.
Correlate with CT morphology, history, timing, prior imaging and plausible inflammatory causes; state uncertainty and recommend appropriate clinical correlation.
Ignore the CT component.
Use SUV alone to assign stage.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDG uptake is not tumour-specific. Anatomic correlation and clinical context are needed, and calibrated differential/uncertainty avoids a false-positive conclusion.

practiceQuestions.stem: A new small pulmonary focus appears on a follow-up oncologic CT, but its nature is uncertain and it was not included in baseline target-lesion sum. What should the learner emphasize?

options.text: Declare metastatic progression solely because it is new.
Review technical comparability and prior imaging, assess whether it is unequivocally malignant in the relevant framework, and describe uncertainty/next appropriate evaluation.
Measure it with ultrasound.
Convert the finding directly into treatment advice.

practiceQuestions.rationale: New lesions require careful verification and context; RECIST provides rules for unequivocal new malignant disease and equivocal findings. The radiology learner should not leap from uncertain imaging to treatment advice.

practiceQuestions.stem: A trainee is asked to assign a cancer stage solely from a cross-sectional scan without clinical/pathology context. What is the best response?

options.text: Assign a definitive stage in every report.
Describe imaging findings and limitations, identify what clinical/pathologic information is needed, and avoid claiming a definitive stage when not supported.
Use patient age as a substitute for missing information.
Do not issue any report.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The course emphasizes imaging findings and stage-relevant observations with appropriate limits; stage group can depend on clinical and pathology data beyond imaging.

practiceQuestions.stem: A contrast reaction occurs during a fictional imaging scenario. Which source should guide up-to-date educational review of contrast reaction and safety principles?

options.text: A social media post without citations.
The current ACR Manual on Contrast Media, alongside local emergency protocols and supervising clinicians.
An old video as a substitute for hospital protocol.
The RECIST guideline.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The current ACR manual is an authoritative open reference, but an independent educational course does not authorize management; local policies and trained clinical supervision govern.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes the BIDMC/DFCI Cancer Imaging Fellowship from board certification?

options.text: Completion of self-study grants ABR certification.

The fellowship is a one-year clinical educational programme; the official page specifies radiology board eligibility/certification for U.S. applicants, while ABR certification has separate training/exam rules.
Cancer imaging is itself an ABMS primary specialty board by virtue of the programme name.
Every cancer imaging fellowship participant automatically qualifies for ABNM certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The programme page states a clinical fellowship and radiology eligibility prerequisite. ABR DR certification requires separate training and examinations; no cancer-imaging-specific board examination is identified by the sources reviewed.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which claim about the optional PET-CT Clinical Fellowship rotation is supported by the public programme page?

options.text: It is an optional clinical rotation with advanced oncology PET-CT/molecular imaging exposure, not proof of separate nuclear-medicine board eligibility.
It grants an NRC Authorized User status by itself.
It replaces supervised nuclear medicine patient-care requirements.
It guarantees therapeutic radiopharmaceutical competence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The programme describes an optional clinical PET-CT rotation; ABNM/NRC pathways require defined training, experience and attestation, not inferred from a rotation label or self-study.

practiceQuestions.stem: A teaching team wants to reuse images from Radiopaedia in a monetized/paywalled school. What is the safe licensing conclusion?

options.text: All images are free for unrestricted commercial reuse.
Link to the source; its stated CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 does not automatically permit commercial or paywalled reuse, so obtain appropriate permission before reproducing.
Remove author names and reuse.
Use screenshots without attribution.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Radiopaedia states CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 subject to Terms and flags commercial/paywalled course use as not automatically permitted. Linking is not the same as copying/rehosting.

title: Cardiothoracic Imaging Fellowship
prerequisites: Advanced learner: prior medical-school-level anatomy, physiology and pathology.
For meaningful board-domain study: completed or concurrent supervised DR-level foundational physics and cross-sectional imaging education.
This is not appropriate as a substitute for medical school, accredited residency, supervised CMR/CT/contrast training, local MRI safety instruction or clinical credentialing.
Ability to use linked resources lawfully; do not download/rehost images unless the named dataset license permits it and attribution/terms are met.
objectives: Use a question-first and technical-adequacy-first approach to chest, vascular and cardiac imaging study.
Describe chest radiographic, CT and HRCT patterns with distribution, associated findings and calibrated uncertainty.
Distinguish incidental-nodule guidance from screening reporting and retain guideline population limits.
Apply source-backed report checklists for suspected PE and acute aortic syndrome in fictional simulations.
Explain CCTA/CMR acquisition and interpretation concepts while preserving clinical and credentialing boundaries.
Produce structured, comparison-aware, finding-first simulated reports and escalation language.
Use authentic de-identified research images ethically with license, attribution and no-reidentification constraints.
Recognize that public ABR domain alignment is not ABR eligibility, a separate cardiothoracic board credential or a passing predictor.

units.title: Safe cardiothoracic image acquisition, dose and anatomic orientation
objectives: Relate clinical question to radiography, CT, CTA, MR or V/Q selection without issuing patient-specific orders.
Recognize why protocol, contrast safety, radiation optimization and image adequacy precede interpretation.
Identify major thoracic and cardiac radiographic/CT landmarks and name limitations from motion, phase and reconstruction.
boardDomains: ABR DR Core: Radiography/Fluoroscopy; CT; Physics; Noninterpretive Skills
units.casePractice: Use only the TCIA technical metadata and authentic source images to describe acquisition, not to make a patient-care recommendation.
units.assessment: Technical-adequacy checklist plus a 200-word contrast/radiation safety reflection referenced to the ACR manual.

units.title: Chest radiography, ICU and emergency pattern reasoning
objectives: Apply a reproducible chest-radiograph search pattern.

units.title: Airspace, infection and micronodular disease

Compare edema, infection, aspiration and inflammatory patterns using explicit imaging evidence.
Recognize when imaging description should prompt urgent clinical correlation rather than autonomous management.

units.casePractice: Use images only within the source viewer; make no local case bank and do not rehost source images.
units.assessment: Pattern-to-differential table for six fictional vignettes, graded for distribution language, uncertainty and urgency.

units.title: HRCT diffuse lung and airway disease
objectives: Use a distribution-first HRCT description: axial, craniocaudal, central/peripheral, and associated findings.

units.casePractice: Use LIDC-IDRI only for CT review skills; it is not an ILD reference standard. Do not claim a diagnosis from an isolated image.

units.title: Pulmonary nodules, lung cancer screening and staging boundaries
objectives: Differentiate incidental-nodule guidance from a screening reporting system.

units.title: Mediastinum, pleura, chest wall and thoracic procedures

units.title: Pulmonary vascular imaging and acute aortic syndromes
objectives: Match suspected-PE scenarios to the ACR appropriateness variants at a conceptual level.

units.title: Cardiac CT and coronary CTA

units.title: Cardiovascular MR, viability, pericardium and masses

units.assessment: Sequence-purpose matching exercise and fictional mass/thrombus differential report with explicit uncertainty.

units.title: Integrated reporting, multidisciplinary collaboration, research and quality

units.title: Thoracic oncology, transplant and post-treatment imaging

assignment.title: Cardiothoracic imaging simulated case-and-report portfolio

boardNames: American Board of Radiology (ABR) – Diagnostic Radiology (DR)
medical.boardStatus: No separate ABR cardiothoracic-imaging subspecialty certificate or examination is listed by ABR. This course maps to publicly named DR Core domains only (Thoracic Radiology, Cardiovascular Imaging, CT, MR, Radiography/Fluoroscopy, Physics and Noninterpretive Skills); it is not an official ABR blueprint or exam preparation product.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABR DR initial certification requires specified clinical training, a four-year ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited DR residency (or an ABR alternate pathway), examinations and a valid license. Emory’s actual fellowship applicants must complete an ACGME-accredited U.S. or Canadian radiology residency, be able to obtain a full unrestricted Georgia license, and be board eligible/certified. This independent self-study does none of those things and does not confer fellowship appointment, board eligibility, certification, licensure, radiation-safety authorization, clinical privileges or a guarantee of passing any exam.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This is an actual, distinct Emory fellowship programme, not a directory category. Its public page describes rotations at Emory University Hospital, Emory Clinic, Emory University Hospital Midtown, Emory Saint Joseph’s Hospital and Grady Memorial Hospital: outpatient/ICU chest radiography, inpatient/outpatient thoracic CT, CT/MR vascular/aorta, cardiac CT/MR, HRCT ILD/airways, and Grady trauma/acute chest-pain CTA/CTPA/lung screening exposure. These are clinical rotations—not video lectures—and this independent course does not reproduce them. Emory’s overview says the department has both ACGME-accredited and non-accredited fellowships in aggregate; it does not state the individual cardiothoracic fellowship’s accreditation status, so none is claimed here.
sourceCaveats: Programme facts come from Emory’s official page. The page describes clinical experience, but not a complete public lecture catalogue, individual programme accreditation status, case volumes or didactic hours.

ABR public content domains are broad category alignment, not an exact blueprint, content weighting, exam leak, endorsement or guarantee. ABR’s current listed DR/IR subspecialty certificates do not include cardiothoracic imaging.
The user outline contained nuclear-medicine/theranostic claims and unverified volume/eligibility assertions. They are outside this cardiothoracic imaging entry and were not imported.

Free-to-view YouTube lectures are linked, not rehosted. Provider/channel identity is reported exactly as displayed; apart from named society/institution channels, no institutional affiliation is inferred.
Guidelines may change. Clinical decisions require current local protocols and qualified clinicians.

Public source material was checked on 2026-10-07; dynamic pages and external video availability may change. Historical STR curriculum and older lectures are used as topic scaffolds, not treated as current clinical guidance.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult has low/intermediate pretest probability for pulmonary embolism and a negative D-dimer. Which statement best reflects the ACR Suspected Pulmonary Embolism narrative for initial imaging?

options.text: CTPA is usually appropriate.
V/Q scanning is usually appropriate.
Both CTPA and V/Q are usually not appropriate.
CTA triple-rule-out is usually appropriate.

practiceQuestions.rationale: For this specific variant, the ACR table rates CTPA and V/Q as usually not appropriate. This question tests source application, not patient-specific care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has a positive D-dimer with low/intermediate pretest probability of PE. Which pair is rated “Usually Appropriate” for initial imaging in the cited ACR narrative?

options.text: CTPA and V/Q scan
CT chest without contrast and echocardiography
CTA triple rule out and catheter pulmonary angiography
Chest radiography and MRI chest

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACR variant table rates CTPA and V/Q scan as usually appropriate in this setting. Actual modality selection depends on patient factors and supervising clinicians.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional CT report mentions a pulmonary nodule on a diagnostic chest CT obtained for another reason. Which framework should not be substituted automatically for an incidental-nodule guideline?

options.text: Fleischner incidental-nodule guideline
Lung-RADS screening reporting system
Comparison with prior imaging
Morphology and measurement documentation

practiceQuestions.rationale: Lung-RADS is a lung CT screening reporting system; the Fleischner 2017 guideline addresses incidentally detected nodules. The clinical context determines which framework applies.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description matches the CDC page’s cited USPSTF annual LDCT screening population recommendation?

options.text: Any adult with cough, regardless of smoking history
Adults 50–80 years with at least 20 pack-years who currently smoke or quit within 15 years
Adults younger than 50 years with any family history
All adults with an incidental nodule

practiceQuestions.rationale: The CDC page states that population recommendation and also describes harms; it is not an individual eligibility decision made by this course.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional CTA shows an acute aortic process. Which report element is explicitly listed in the ACC/AHA guideline’s essential CT/MR aortic report elements?

options.text: Only the largest axial diameter, without method
Extension into branch vessels and suspected end-organ injury
A mandatory exact surgical plan
A PET uptake score

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline asks for branch-vessel extension, potential end-organ injury, and other structured elements. Imaging reports support, but do not replace, multidisciplinary treatment decisions.

practiceQuestions.stem: Why can ECG-gated CT be useful when assessing the aortic root and ascending aorta?

options.text: It eliminates the need for image reconstruction.
It decreases motion artifact and improves measurement precision/confidence.
It replaces contrast assessment in every patient.
It proves the cause of all chest pain.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACC/AHA guideline states ECG-gating decreases root/ascending-aortic motion artifact and increases precision and diagnostic confidence.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best reflects the cited ACR contrast manual?

options.text: All contrast adverse events are allergic reactions.
Allergic-like and physiologic reactions are distinct categories, and injectors must be prepared to recognize/manage adverse events under policy.
Severe reactions are impossible with modern iodinated contrast.
This course authorizes independent reaction treatment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACR manual distinguishes allergic-like from physiologic reactions and emphasizes preparedness. It does not turn self-study into authorization or local protocol training.

practiceQuestions.stem: In the SCMR 2020 protocol update, which sequence family is described as the method of choice for cine imaging because of high signal-to-noise and myocardium-blood-pool contrast?

options.text: bSSFP cine
Non-ECG-gated chest CT
Planar radiography
V/Q perfusion imaging

practiceQuestions.rationale: The SCMR document identifies bSSFP as the method of choice for cine imaging, with stated artifact alternatives at 3T.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes the ABR status of a cardiothoracic imaging fellowship in this independent study course?

options.text: It automatically grants a separate ABR cardiothoracic subspecialty certificate.
It replaces an ACGME/RCPSC diagnostic radiology residency.
Cardiothoracic imaging is relevant to DR Core domains, but ABR’s listed DR/IR subspecialties do not include a cardiothoracic imaging certificate.
Watching the videos makes a learner ABR board eligible.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABR publicly lists neuroradiology, nuclear radiology, pediatric radiology and pain medicine for DR/IR subspecialties; cardiothoracic imaging is not listed. The DR Core description includes thoracic and cardiovascular imaging.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is supported by Emory’s official fellowship page?

options.text: The fellowship is a residency that confers a medical license.
Applicants must have completed an ACGME-accredited U.S. or Canadian radiology residency, obtain a full unrestricted Georgia license, and be board eligible/certified.
The page promises a separate ABR cardiothoracic examination.
The listed rotations are online lectures only.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Emory’s programme page states those applicant criteria and describes clinical rotations. That does not make this independent course affiliated with Emory or a substitute for clinical training.
